title: Vector algebra, vector calculus, linear algebra `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Boas Ch. 3, Ch. 6 — do all end-of-chapter problems, not a sample. This is asked directly in JAM and used constantly after.
videoDepthNote: Watch every video under this playlist's Linear Algebra + Vector Calculus sub-section (use the playlist's own video titles to find them — it's organized by sub-topic, not chronological upload order). Skip any video titled as a PYQ-solution walkthrough for now — come back to those after you've done the concept videos.
notes:
**Why full depth now:** Eigenvalues/diagonalization and vector calculus identities are used everywhere afterward — mechanics, EM, QM. No shortcut version exists.
**Correction from v1:** Small oscillations & normal modes was previously deferred as JEST-only. It's actually grouped with core mechanics in JAM/JEST overlap and rated high-yield (uses the same eigenvalue machinery from Topic 1) — see it under **Phase A-Bonus #7** below, do it right after this topic if you're on pace.
prerequisites: None — this is the starting topic.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM: direct diagonalization/eigenvalue NAT & MCQ, vector identity proofs. JEST: same tools embedded inside mechanics/EM/QM problems rather than asked standalone.

title: Linear differential equations `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Boas Ch. 8 — full chapter (JAM asks first-order + constant-coefficient second-order; JEST's syllabus doesn't demand much beyond this).
videoDepthNote: Just the ODE-technique videos (separable, linear, exact, constant-coefficient 2nd order). No need for series-solution videos yet — that comes with special functions later (Phase B).
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST: solve a given ODE, classify its type, apply the initial condition.

title: Complex analysis — basic part only `[JAM-partial]`
book: Boas Ch. 14, sections 1–4 only (complex number algebra, polar form, basic functions). **Stop before residues/contour integration** — that's JEST-only, deferred to Phase B.
videoDepthNote: Watch only the intro complex-numbers video(s), skip the residue/contour-integration videos for now.
notes: **Why partial:** JAM only tests complex number algebra. Full residue calculus is JEST-specific — doing it now would be premature since you won't use it before Feb anyway.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST (basic level only): complex algebra, polar form, basic function evaluation MCQ/NAT. Residues deferred to Phase A-Bonus #4.

title: Fourier series `[JAM+JEST]` (Fourier/Laplace *transforms* are `[JEST-only]` — see Phase B)
book: Boas Ch. 7, Fourier series sections only.
videoDepthNote: Watch the Fourier *series* videos only (periodic function expansions, even/odd). Skip the Fourier *transform* and Laplace transform videos — defer those.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST: expand a given periodic function, find a specific coefficient, use even/odd symmetry shortcuts.

title: Newton's laws, conservation, collisions `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Kleppner & Kolenkow, full relevant chapters.
videoDepthNote: Roughly lectures 1–10 of this 38-lecture series cover Newtonian mechanics, conservation laws, and collisions. You do **not** need to watch all 38 — this playlist also covers heat/waves/stat mech later, which you'll come back to separately (see Topic 12 below).
prerequisites: None — independent of the Topic 1–4 math track.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM: standard collision/conservation numericals. JEST: same, sometimes with a constraint or non-inertial twist.

title: Generalized coordinates, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Goldstein, Ch. 1–2 (Lagrangian) + Ch. 8 (Hamiltonian, up to Hamilton's equations — skip Hamilton-Jacobi theory, that's grad-level beyond both JAM and JEST).
videoDepthNote: Roughly lectures 11–19 cover this. Watch these fully — this is the conceptual core of the subject.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM: set up the Lagrangian for a given constrained system, derive the EOM. JEST: same, plus Hamiltonian/canonical-momentum questions.

title: Central force problem, Kepler problem `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Goldstein, central force chapter.
video: Balakrishnan, Classical Physics (NPTEL) — https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL5E4E56893588CBA8 (within the same 11–19 lecture range, or nearby)
videoDepthNote: Full — Kepler's laws derivation from the Lagrangian is a near-guaranteed problem type in both exams.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST: derive the orbit equation, effective potential, Kepler's laws from the Lagrangian.

title: Special relativity — basic part `[JAM-partial]`
book: Any standard "Modern Physics" chapter covering postulates, time dilation, length contraction, mass-energy equivalence (this is JAM-level; you likely already have a book for this from general M.Sc-entrance prep).
video: Search within Balakrishnan's playlist or Pravegaa's Modern Physics section for the SR basics.
videoDepthNote: Just the postulates + kinematics + E=mc² level. The 4-vector / Lagrangian-in-relativity treatment JEST wants is deferred to Phase B.
notes: **Correction from v1:** the blueprint's chapter data flags SR (mechanics) as "frequently tested," not a rare add-on — so the full treatment is now a Phase A-Bonus candidate (**#6** below) rather than sitting untouched in Phase B until March/April.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM: time dilation / length contraction / E=mc² numericals. Full 4-vector treatment deferred to Phase A-Bonus #6.

title: Electrostatics, magnetostatics — basic part `[JAM-partial]`
book: Griffiths Ch. 2–3 (electrostatics), Ch. 5 (magnetostatics) — read for concepts and Gauss's/Ampere's law applications. **Skip boundary value problems (Laplace's equation, method of images) and multipole expansion for now** — JEST-only, Phase B.
videoDepthNote: Watch the electrostatics/magnetostatics fundamentals videos only.
notes: **Note:** boundary value problems + method of images + multipole expansion is the single highest-rated chapter in the whole EM section by frequency and weightage — see **Phase A-Bonus #3**. Do it as soon as this topic is done, before it's forgotten.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM: Gauss's/Ampere's law applications, field calculations for standard geometries. Boundary value problems deferred to Phase A-Bonus #3.

title: Faraday's law, time-varying fields, displacement current, Maxwell's equations `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Griffiths Ch. 7 (up to Maxwell's equations — full form, differential and integral).
videoDepthNote: Full — this is core to both exams.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST: apply/derive Maxwell's equations in integral and differential form, induced-EMF problems.

title: Plane EM wave propagation, reflection, refraction `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Griffiths Ch. 9 (up through reflection/transmission at normal incidence — skip oblique incidence and dispersive/conducting media derivations for now).
videoDepthNote: Watch the plane-wave and basic reflection/refraction videos.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST: derive the wave equation from Maxwell's equations, normal-incidence reflection/transmission coefficients.

title: Diffraction, interference, polarization `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Griffiths' brief optics coverage + any standard optics chapter (Hecht, if you want more problems) — single/double slit, basic polarization (Malus's law), interference conditions.
videoDepthNote: Full — this is standard UG-level optics, asked in both exams at similar depth.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST: slit-pattern numericals, Malus's law, standard interference-condition problems.

title: Uncertainty principle, Schrödinger equation, central potentials, hydrogen atom `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Griffiths QM, Ch. 1–2 (Schrödinger eq., particle in a box, harmonic oscillator), Ch. 4 (hydrogen atom, angular momentum basics up to the radial equation).
videoDepthNote: Watch fully through the hydrogen atom lectures. This is the single highest-value QM block for JAM and the entry point for JEST's deeper QM (Phase B).
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM: particle-in-a-box / harmonic-oscillator eigenvalue problems. JEST: same, plus the hydrogen-atom radial equation and angular-momentum basics.

title: Laws of thermodynamics, thermodynamic potentials, kinetic theory, Maxwell's relations `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Garg, Bansal, Ghosh, *Thermal Physics* — thermodynamics + kinetic theory chapters, full.
videoDepthNote: Full — this section is tested almost identically in both exams.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST: derive/apply a Maxwell relation, kinetic-theory numericals, thermodynamic-potential problems.

title: Classical and quantum statistics — basic definitions `[JAM-partial]`
book: Garg, Bansal, Ghosh — Maxwell-Boltzmann, Fermi-Dirac, Bose-Einstein distribution *definitions and basic properties* (skip full partition-function derivations and deep Fermi/Bose gas applications for now).
videoDepthNote: The intro distributions videos only.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM: identify/apply the correct distribution for a given system. Full partition-function derivations deferred to Phase A-Bonus #5.

title: Black body radiation `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Garg, Bansal, Ghosh or any Modern Physics chapter — Planck's law derivation, Wien's/Stefan-Boltzmann laws.
videoDepthNote: Full — standard derivation, asked in both.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST: Planck's-law limiting cases, Wien's/Stefan-Boltzmann numericals.

title: Semiconductor basics, p-n junctions, diodes, transistors `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Millman & Halkias — semiconductor physics, diode, and BJT chapters.
videoDepthNote: Full — JAM's electronics section overlaps closely with this.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST: diode/BJT characteristic-curve reading, basic device-physics MCQs.

title: LCR circuits, rectifiers, amplifiers, OPAMPs, digital electronics — basic level `[JAM+JEST]`
book: Millman & Halkias — circuits, rectifier, and basic op-amp chapters; any standard digital logic chapter for gates.
videoDepthNote: Full for rectifiers, basic amplifiers, standard op-amp configurations (inverting/non-inverting/summing), and logic gates. **Skip active filters and oscillator design derivations for now** — those get more JEST-specific attention in Phase B.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST: circuit-analysis numericals, op-amp configuration identification, logic-gate truth tables.

title: Crystal structure, reciprocal lattice, basic band theory `[JAM+JEST]` — NEW, corrects a gap in v1
book: Kittel, *Introduction to Solid State Physics* — crystal structure, reciprocal lattice/Bragg condition, and an intro pass at band theory (free electron model, origin of band gaps). Stop before phonon dispersion and deep band-structure derivations — those are Phase B.
video: pick whichever NPTEL Solid State Physics playlist matches your current book's chapter order; skip straight to crystal structure + free-electron/band-basics lectures.
videoDepthNote: Enough to comfortably answer a Bragg-condition NAT or a "why does a gap open at the zone boundary" conceptual MCQ.
notes:
**Why this is here:** Solid State Physics was entirely absent from v1, but it's a real chunk of the JEST paper (crystal structure and basic band theory specifically sit in the JAM+JEST overlap zone, not the JEST-exclusive tail). Skipping it wasn't a deliberate deferral, it was a blind spot.
**Depth:** Enough to comfortably answer a Bragg-condition NAT or a "why does a gap open at the zone boundary" conceptual MCQ.
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST: Bragg-condition NATs, "why does a gap open at the zone boundary" conceptual MCQs.

title: Basic atomic structure, nuclear models, radioactivity `[JAM+JEST]` — NEW, corrects a gap in v1
book: Arthur Beiser, *Concepts of Modern Physics* — Bohr model and its limitations, basic term symbols/selection rules (light touch, full depth deferred), nuclear models (liquid drop, shell model basics), radioactive decay law.
video: any standard Modern Physics playlist covering the same chapters — no need for a dedicated series here, this is a short, book-driven topic.
videoDepthNote: Enough for a half-life NAT and a basic term-symbol MCQ. Fine structure detail and full atomic spectra depth are deferred (Phase B).
notes:
**Why this is here:** same issue as above — Atomic/Molecular/Nuclear/Particle Physics is a real ~6–10% weightage subject that had zero entries in v1. The basic-structure and nuclear-models part overlaps with JAM; particle physics proper is JEST-only and deferred (Phase B, low priority).
**Depth:** Enough for a half-life NAT and a basic term-symbol MCQ. Fine structure detail and full atomic spectra depth are deferred (Phase B).
typicalQuestionStyle: JAM/JEST: Bohr-model numericals, half-life/decay-law NATs, basic term-symbol MCQs.
